description.value: The people the test data is about.
Organizations the definitions refer to.
The episode of care the plan is delivered under, and that every record of care refers back to.
The plan as delivered to the patient: the care plan, the service requests it consists of, and the care team responsible.
What the patient submitted: the measurements and the questionnaire responses.

The clinical record: the diagnosis each episode addresses, and the triage result of each submission. The impressions are not loaded — automated processing creates them, and the ones here record what it should produce.
One Provenance per submission, naming the resources submitted together. This is what triggers automated processing.
The assessment task raised with each triage result. Not loaded either, and its priority is the triage colour.
The plan, the activities it is built from, the questionnaire and the automated-processing rules.
Settings the loader reads before it loads anything. Not test data, and not created on the target.

Pulse submitted under the completed episode. 118/min falls in the upper yellow range of 110 to 130, so triage returns yellow and raises a task with priority urgent.
Oxygen saturation submitted under the completed episode. 84% is at or below the red absolute range of 85%, so triage returns red and raises a task with priority asap.

Triages a submitted observation against absolute thresholds expressed in the observation's own unit. Reads the reference ranges from the observation it is given, so a measurement must carry them to be assessed; a GAL range yields a yellow assessment and a RAL range a red one.

Triages a submitted questionnaire response by matching each answer against the answer-significance mappings on the questionnaire, and recording one finding basis per answered question alongside the overall assessment.
